meta.purpose: Every question that has to be answered before a decision is reasonable, split into four states: answered from a source, answerable by us and not yet done, answerable only by the account holder, and unanswerable with current access. The point is to stop a decision being made on a guess.

states.answered: Answered, quoted and linked to an official source.
states.open-doable: Can be answered from here; not yet done. Each has an owner action.
states.account-holder: Can only be answered from inside the Associates dashboard or the Amazon account.
states.blocked: Cannot be answered with any access this project has. Recorded so it is not silently assumed.

questions.question: What exact wording does Amazon require an associate to display?
questions.answer: “As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.” The Agreement requires it be stated clearly and prominently on the Site.

questions.question: May this site show prices, stock or star ratings?
questions.answer: Only where Amazon serves the link carrying that data, or where it arrives through the Creators API or PA API. No such feed is connected, so nothing of the kind is published anywhere on this site.

questions.question: What is an ASIN, and is the code in a supplied short link one?
questions.answer: An ASIN is “a unique 10-character alphanumeric code assigned to every product listed in the Amazon store”, and it appears after /dp/ in a product URL. All five supplied codes are 9 characters, so they are short-link slugs, not ASINs. The shop uses the 10-character /dp/ code observed on the destination page and keeps the supplied slug in a separate field.
questions.source_label: Amazon Seller Central blog, Understanding ASINs (Jun 4, 2025)

questions.question: How must affiliate links be marked for search engines?
questions.answer: Google asks that advertisements or paid placements be marked with rel="sponsored"; multiple rel values may be combined. Every outbound Amazon link on this site carries rel="sponsored nofollow noopener".
questions.source_label: Google Search Central, Qualify your outbound links (last updated 2025-12-10)

questions.question: Where must the affiliate disclosure appear, and how prominently?
questions.answer: The FTC asks for disclosures that are clear and conspicuous, and says a connection between an endorser and a marketer should be disclosed where it will be seen. On this site the statement sits in a strip directly under the masthead on every page and is repeated in the footer, so it precedes the first buy link.
questions.source_label: FTC Endorsement Guides: What People Are Asking

questions.question: What are the official safe minimum internal cooking temperatures?
questions.answer: Poultry 165°F; ground meats 160°F; whole cuts of beef, pork, veal and lamb 145°F with a three-minute rest; fish and shellfish 145°F; leftovers and casseroles 165°F.
questions.source_label: USDA FSIS, Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (updated Apr 14, 2025)

questions.question: Do the five supplied links resolve to identifiable Amazon product pages?
questions.answer: Yes, all five, observed on 2026-11-20. They resolve to B0CDY277D3, B09B7SB46R, B08DKYBTPH, B0DHZTCNR5 and B0DZFD6R9Z. This supersedes the earlier finding that one link (B0c8moW59) never resolved.
questions.source_label: Destination page reached from https://link.amazon/B0c8moW59 (the link previously recorded as unresolved)

questions.question: Is each link attributed to tracking ID shopnow047c-20?
questions.answer: Unanswered. No supplied link visibly carried the tag parameter, and no Associates report exists to check a click against. Cannot be answered from outside the account.
questions.how_to_answer: Open the Associates dashboard, click one link, and confirm the click appears under shopnow047c-20 in the tracking report. One link, one product, before scaling.
questions.source_label: Program Policies, section 2(b) — Associates ID must appear as a parameter

questions.question: Are the supplied link.amazon short links compliant Special Links?
questions.answer: Unresolved, and deliberately not adjudicated. No official Amazon page addresses this host by name, and the behaviour is only observable on click while signed in. This site does not claim they are valid, and does not claim they are invalid. Every buy button on this site therefore points at a direct, tagged amazon.com/dp/ URL instead.
questions.how_to_answer: Run the one-link test signed in to the Associates account and record the destination and the tracking report result with a date.
questions.source_label: Operating Agreement, section 1 — links must use the tagged link formats provided

questions.question: What commission rate applies to home and kitchen categories?
questions.answer: Unknown. The rate card sits behind the Associates sign-in, so no rate is published or used in any calculation on this site. No revenue figure or forecast appears anywhere.
questions.how_to_answer: Read the Commission Income Statement while signed in, and record the rates with the date read.
questions.source_label: Commission Income Statement, section 3 and Appendix

questions.question: Has the Associates account been approved and is it in good standing?
questions.answer: Unknown from here. An account that has not made a qualifying sale within the programme's stated window can be closed, which would make every link on this site inert.
questions.how_to_answer: Check the account status page in Associates Central and note the date.
questions.source_label: Operating Agreement, section 6 — term and termination

questions.question: Which editorial topics bring qualified search traffic?
questions.answer: Not yet known. The three live guides are question-shaped hypotheses chosen for a real decision, not for measured demand. No keyword or volume data has been obtained, and none is claimed.
questions.how_to_answer: Once analytics and Search Console exist, pick the next topic from the queries that actually arrive. Until then, publish one guide per week on the calendar and mark each as a hypothesis.
questions.source_label: Google Search Central — Search Console: monitor and debug

questions.question: Does the disclosure strip actually sit above the first buy link on every page?
questions.answer: Yes, and it is now machine-checked on every build rather than trusted: _tools/shop_check.py fails if any page has the disclosure after the first outbound product link, or missing entirely.
questions.how_to_answer: Run python3 _tools/shop_check.py. It is part of the deploy workflow.

questions.question: What did readers actually do — how many arrived, read, and clicked?
questions.answer: Unmeasured. There is no analytics collector on the site, no cookie and no tag. GitHub Pages serves static files only, so there is nowhere in this repository for a collector to run. A measurement plan exists; a measurement does not.
questions.how_to_answer: Deploy a first-party collector on a host that can run a process, or accept a privacy-respecting hosted analytics service and disclose it. Then record the five defined events.
questions.source_label: GitHub Docs — GitHub Pages is a static hosting service

questions.question: Do the appliances perform as their listings claim?
questions.answer: Unknown. This project has not tested any appliance, and will not repeat performance claims as its own. Listing language is reproduced and labelled as the seller's.
questions.how_to_answer: Physically test each machine, record method and date, or continue to publish listing claims as claims. There is no shortcut.
questions.source_label: FTC — an endorsement must reflect the endorser's honest experience

questions.question: Is this site findable as one site rather than several competing ones?
questions.answer: Now yes, in structure: shop/ publishes its own sitemap, RSS feed and robots.txt, every page declares a canonical URL, and the robots.txt at the repository root names both the shop sitemap and the older sections' sitemaps. Two older sections still exist and are listed on the Site map page so they can be retired deliberately rather than by accident.
questions.how_to_answer: Confirm Search Console sees one property with the shop as the canonical set after the first crawl.
questions.source_label: Google Search Central — how to consolidate duplicate URLs with canonicals
